newsitem.title: USA: Chiron seeks approval of melanoma drug.
newsitem.headline: Chiron seeks approval of melanoma drug.

text.p: Chiron Corp said it applied to the Food and Drug Administration for approval of its Proleukin drug to treat metastatic melanoma.
The drug is currently approved as a treatment for metastatic renal cell carcinoma and last September it received orphan drug status for the treatment of metastatic melanoma.

"We believed that Proleukin immunotherapy represents a significant advance in therapeutic options for the treatment of metastatic melanoma," Dr. Bruce Scharschmidt, vice president of clinical affairs at Chiron, said in a statement.

"Clinical studies performed to date have demonstrated that (it) can produce durable responses, where some patients have remained disease free for eight years or more. These are clinically impressive results in a deadly disease where the patient prognosis is often only a few months."
The company said the toxicity of the drug was severe, but also "manageable and rapidly reversible in most cases."
